title: 8004: Bring Agents On Chain
description:
8004 is a draft Ethereum standard for AI agents. It defines registries for identity, reputation and validation, and feedback has to come from someone other than the agent's owner. A live example is a token agent on Arc that any AI client can query over MCP. At 8004scan we index these registries, and the hard part is deciding what the numbers mean.
On 25 October we counted 1,524,713 agents on 27 mainnets. BNB Chain had 23% of them and Ethereum mainnet had 2%. With its L2s, Ethereum had 75% of agents and 92% of feedback. In five days, Base went from 222,000 agents to over a million and Ethereum's feedback per agent fell from 2.00 to 0.64. Our July health check found 8,631 healthy agents, 2.24% of those registered.
Every metric we publish has five fields: what it measures, numerator, denominator, observation time and known limits. Alpharc, a market we run on Robinhood Chain, Arc and Base, uses the same idea. Trading calls there are rated by other users' verified onchain trades.
abstract: 8004 is the Ethereum standard that gives AI agents an onchain identity. At 8004scan we index every registration, and the numbers change a lot depending on how you count. On 25 October we saw 1,524,713 agents on 27 mainnets. BNB Chain had 23% of them and Ethereum mainnet had 2%. Add its L2s and Ethereum had 75% of agents and 92% of all feedback. I'll show how we define each metric and how the choice of denominator changes which chain looks like the leader.
